title: Raise TermAl process FD limit before spawning agent runtimes
outcome: The shared Codex app-server reached 253 descriptors under the inherited macOS soft RLIMIT_NOFILE of 256, so delegated review could not spawn git and aborted with EMFILE. TermAl should raise its own Unix soft descriptor limit early so the app-server and all subsequently spawned agents inherit adequate capacity. This is distinct from the Rust test-gate wrapper and must not require users to launch TermAl through ulimit.
acceptance: On Unix, TermAl raises RLIMIT_NOFILE before spawning app-server or agent children without lowering an existing limit. If the requested value cannot be reached, startup reports the requested, effective, and applicable ceiling values; macOS kernel-ceiling rejection degrades to the best achievable lift instead of leaving the original low limit. TERMAL_NOFILE_LIMIT has a documented safe maximum. Tests deterministically cover default, valid override, invalid override, capping, no-lowering, and syscall-failure behavior without requiring a host-specific setrlimit success. Windows remains unchanged. Architecture, test, and shared-Codex documentation cross-link the runtime and harness policies. All focused and repository quality gates pass.

completion.summary: Raised Unix process soft descriptor capacity early before runtime spawning, with capped override, no lowering/hard-limit changes, macOS ceiling-aware best-achievable fallback, honest final readback diagnostics, Windows noop,27 deterministic tests and cross-linked policy docs.
